stem: During a federal controlled-substance inventory, which counting approaches are consistent with 21 CFR 1304.11(e)(6)? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Estimate an opened Schedule II bottle whenever the pharmacist believes the estimate is close.
Estimate every opened Schedule III-V container regardless of size.
Use an exact count or measure for Schedule II inventory.
An opened Schedule III-V container may generally be estimated when it does not hold more than 1,000 units.
Use an exact count for an opened Schedule III-V container holding more than 1,000 units.

explanation.core_reasoning: Federal inventory counting is schedule- and container-size specific. Schedule II requires exact counting or measuring; opened Schedule III-V containers may generally be estimated unless the container holds more than 1,000 units.

choice_analysis.A: Schedule II does not use the general opened-container estimation allowance.
choice_analysis.B: The over-1,000-unit exception prevents a blanket estimation rule for every III-V container.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. Schedule II inventory requires exact count or measure.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. This is the general estimation allowance for opened III-V containers at or below the threshold.
choice_analysis.E: Correct. The larger opened III-V container must be counted exactly.

related_facts: Amphetamine/dextroamphetamine products are Schedule II and therefore fall under the exact-count rule.
Alprazolam is Schedule IV; whether estimation is permitted depends on the opened-container size threshold.
explanation.mpje_trap: Inventory questions often hinge on two variables at once: schedule and whether an opened III-V container exceeds 1,000 units.

reasoning_steps: Apply the exact-count rule to Schedule II
Apply the 1,000-unit threshold to opened Schedule III-V containers
